claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions.

Let's start with the basics: **Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child - Alex, who's 17 and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex is 17, I need to understand their current situation as this affects eligibility.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, are they in sixth form, college, doing A-levels, or an approved training course?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in sixth form or college or anything like that. They finished school but haven't gone on to do A-levels or any courses.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. Since Alex is 17 and not in approved education or training, I need to ask:

**Has Alex started paid work for 24 hours or more a week, or started claiming any benefits in their own right** (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex hasn't started working that much - they're not doing 24 hours a week or anything. And they're not claiming any benefits themselves either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. One more important question:

**Has Alex registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services since leaving education?** 

(This is relevant because Child Benefit can continue for up to 20 weeks after a 16 or 17 year old leaves education if they register with one of these services.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex hasn't signed up with the careers service or anything like that since leaving school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. I just need to confirm one final detail:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why: While you normally qualify for Child Benefit for children under 16, Alex is 17. For children aged 16-19, you can continue to receive Child Benefit only if they stay in approved education or training (such as A-levels, college, or approved training courses).

Additionally, Child Benefit can continue for up to 20 weeks after a 16 or 17 year old leaves education if they register with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services.

Since Alex:
- Is not in approved education or training
- Has not registered with a careers service or the armed services
- Is not working 24+ hours per week
- Is not claiming benefits in their own right

The eligibility criteria for Child Benefit are not met in this situation.

**If Alex's circumstances change** - for example, if they start an approved course or register with a careers service - you may become eligible at that point and should consider applying then.
